question: What will be the total spending by all Senate candidates in the 2026 US election cycle?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: FEC final Senate-candidate spending in recent cycles (2020 $2.01B, 2022 $1.71B, 2024 $1.69B on the bythenumbers page). The 2026 field had spent $666M by mid-Aug. At 15 months it held a record $383M in cash and had raised 16% more than 2024 at the same point. It had spent less than 2024 by summer (2024 18-month 2-yr disbursements $682M vs 2026 ~$622M through Aug per USAFacts), so 2026 spending is back-loaded. Competitive races (GA, TX, NC, ME, MI, OH, IA, AK; Polymarket 62% D control) point to an eventual total of ~$1.7-1.85B. The December figure will lack Nov 24-Dec 31 spending (year-end report due Jan 2027), and there is a small risk that post-general reports are unprocessed, which skews the low tail. No market prices this quantity directly; only the Polymarket Senate-control contracts (not matching, used as competitiveness context).
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off FEC 'Spending: by the numbers' page (Senate, 2026), total spending by all Senate candidates; fine print allows waiting until Dec 31, 2026. Not off USAFacts/OpenSecrets or independent expenditures.
- Event window: cycle spending Jan 2025 -> whatever the FEC page shows at resolution (Dec 2-31, 2026). As of Now (2026-10-01), the election is on Nov 3; the post-general report (covering through Nov 23) is due Dec 3; the year-end report (Nov 24-Dec 31) is due Jan 31, 2027, so it will NOT be included at resolution.
- FEC page history (question background): 2020 $2,007.6M; 2022 $1,708.2M; 2024 $1,687.3M (final, includes year-end). As of mid-Aug 2026: $666.3M (D $393.9M, R $261.0M, other $11.4M).
- FEC 12-month summary (through Dec 31, 2025): 230 Senate candidates, receipts $454.1M, disbursements $237.9M, cash on hand $345.8M.
- FEC 15-month summary (through Mar 31, 2026): 291 candidates, receipts $654M, disbursements $400.8M, debts $44.6M, cash on hand $382.7M; receipts ~16% above the 2024 field at the same point (FEC page).
- FEC 18-month 2024 cycle (through Jun 30, 2024): receipts $857.5M, disbursements $681.9M, cash on hand $305M. FEC 24-month 2024 (through Dec 31, 2024): disbursements $1.5B (2-yr count; the bythenumbers page shows $1.687B for 2024, so the page appears to count a broader period, possibly the 6-year cycle).
- USAFacts (updated Sep 28, 2026): Senate candidates spent $622M Jan 2025-Aug 2026; Texas $90.2M (Cornyn-Paxton primary/runoff), Georgia $60.8M lead.
- Big war chests as of Jun 30, 2026: Ossoff raised $98M (COH $42.6M); Talarico raised $68.6M (COH $21.5M); Hagerty $16M raised.
- Competitive map: GA, TX, NC, ME, MI, OH special, FL special, IA, NH, AK, NE; Polymarket (Oct 2026) shows the Senate majority as contested.
- Status quo: recent cycles landed at $1.7-2.0B on this page; 2026 spent less than 2024 by mid-cycle but holds more cash and is raising faster.
- Searched but could not find: the FEC 18-month 2025-26 summary (URL 404); whether the bythenumbers page in Dec 2022/Dec 2024 already reflected post-general data; Q3 2026 totals (not filed until Oct 15).
calls.reference_class: FEC 'spending by the numbers' total for all Senate candidates in recent election cycles (2020, 2022, 2024), scaled from mid-cycle spending pace

calls.reasoning: 2022 midterm Senate candidates had $710.6M disbursed by June 30 and finished at $1.708B (~2.4x). 2026 shows $666M by mid-Aug and $654M receipts at 15 months (vs $707M in 2022, $611M in 2024), implying ~$1.6B on 2022's ratio. But the late environment is hotter: AdImpact Senate ad projection $3.4B (+48% vs 2022), record Talarico $30M Q2, huge TX/OH races, Dem cash surge, Polymarket D-control 62% signals many competitive seats. Resolution data likely through post-general reports (excludes December), trimming a few percent; small tail if resolved on pre-general data only. No market found pricing total candidate spending; Polymarket Senate-control markets are only indirect evidence.

calls.reference_class: FEC Senate candidate full-cycle disbursements in 2022 and 2024 midterm/presidential cycles, scaled from same-point partial totals

calls.reasoning: Anchor: FEC Senate-candidate final/partial ratios from 2022 and 2024 applied to 2026's 15-month disbursements ($400.8M) and mid-August page total ($666M) give about $1.55-1.62B. Adjusted up for receipts and cash on hand above 2024 at the same point, a record Texas race, AdImpact's Senate ad projection of +27% versus 2024, and a competitive map. Adjusted down because the December snapshot excludes year-end reports (a few percent). Low tail allows for an early snapshot taken before post-general reports are processed. No market prices this quantity.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) whether the bythenumbers page counts 2-year or multi-year activity. Page and summary figures disagree ($666M vs $622M mid-cycle; the 2024 final of $1.687B vs Run 1's ~$1.5B 24-month figure, which Run 2 describes as receipts), suggesting multi-year counting; so I preferred like-basis ratios, which land around $1.55-1.6B. (2) Resolution timing: post-general reports (due ~Dec 3) are likely included under the Dec 31 wait; year-end reports are not, a few percent below a true final. (3) How large a hot-cycle premium to apply is pure judgment; I took a modest one, putting the median at $1.65B, slightly below the runs' $1.68-1.72B because of the year-end exclusion and the lag in spending to date versus 2024. No web access on this run; all evidence came from the dossiers.
